title: Basketweave Rectangle Wrap
subtitle: Textured front-and-back post treble stitch in a classic woven pattern
excerpt: A chunky rectangular wrap worked in alternating panels of front-post and back-post trebles to create a raised basketweave effect. Aran weight yarn on a 5mm hook gives firm, structured fabric with satisfying depth.
sourceNotes: Original pattern synthesised for Homemade. Basketweave post-stitch construction is a widely established crochet technique with no single source.
heroPrompt: A neatly folded rectangular wrap in warm oatmeal aran yarn with a deep basketweave texture. The raised woven squares catch the light. Soft natural background, overhead flat-lay perspective.

crochet.gaugeText: 14 sts and 10 rows to 10cm over basketweave pattern using 5mm hook. Tension is important for finished size.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approximately 170cm wide x 50cm deep after blocking.

glossaryTerms.definition: Insert the hook from front to back around the post of the stitch below rather than through the top loops, then work a treble crochet. The stitch sits proud on the front of the fabric.
Insert the hook from back to front around the post of the stitch below, then work a treble crochet. The stitch sits proud on the back of the fabric, creating a recessed line on the front.

content.text: This rectangular wrap measures approximately 170cm wide by 50cm deep and is worked from side to side in rows using alternating panels of front-post and back-post trebles. The raised squares interlock to produce the characteristic woven look of basketweave. You work entirely in one piece with no seaming. Aran weight yarn on a 5mm hook produces firm, structured fabric with good drape at the finished dimensions. Post stitches require a firm and even tension: the raised effect depends on wrapping around the post of the stitch in the row below rather than working into the top loops. Practise on a swatch of at least 20 stitches before casting on for the full wrap.

Yarn: approximately 600g of aran weight yarn (100% wool or wool-acrylic blend works well for stitch definition). Hook: 5mm. You will also need a tapestry needle for weaving in ends, scissors, a tape measure, and optional blocking mat and rust-proof pins.

14 stitches and 10 rows to 10cm over basketweave pattern using a 5mm hook. Check your tension against this measurement after working your swatch. A tighter tension will produce a narrower, shorter wrap; a looser tension will produce a wider, longer one.

The wrap is worked from one short end to the other. The foundation chain is the width of the wrap (the 50cm measurement). Each basketweave square is 4 stitches wide and 4 rows tall. The pattern repeat is 8 stitches (4 FPtr + 4 BPtr), so the stitch count must be a multiple of 8 plus 2 edge stitches. A count of 74 stitches gives a finished width close to 50cm at the stated gauge. The length (170cm) is built up over approximately 238 rows.

Note on abbreviations: ch-3 turning chain counts as the first treble throughout. When the pattern says "tr in next st", work into the top loops of that stitch in the normal way. When the pattern says "FPtr" or "BPtr", wrap around the post of the corresponding stitch in the row below.
Ch 76. (This includes 2 turning chains for the first row.)
Ch 3 (counts as first tr), tr in 4th ch from hook and in each ch to end. Turn. (74 sts)
Ch 3 (counts as first tr), tr in next 3 sts, [FPtr around each of next 4 sts, tr in next 4 sts] 8 times, FPtr around each of next 4 sts, tr in top of turning ch. Turn. (74 sts)
Work Rows 2 to 5 four times total to complete the first set of four raised-post rows.
Ch 3 (counts as first tr), [BPtr around each of next 4 sts, tr in next 4 sts] 9 times, BPtr around each of next 4 sts, tr in top of turning ch. Turn. (74 sts)
Work Rows 6 to 9 four times total.
Alternate Block A rows (Rows 2 to 5) with Block B rows (Rows 6 to 9). Continue until the work measures approximately 170cm from the foundation chain. Fasten off, leaving a 15cm tail for weaving in.

Weave in all ends using the tapestry needle, working along the wrong side so nothing is visible from the front. Block the wrap by soaking in cool water, pressing out excess moisture in a towel, then pinning to the stated dimensions on a foam mat. Allow to dry completely before unpinning. Blocking softens the fabric and evens out stitch tension.
Follow the care instructions on your yarn label. Most aran weight wools benefit from hand washing in cool water with a wool-safe detergent. Reshape and dry flat. Do not tumble dry or wring.

Once you are confident with post stitches on a rectangle, consider a ripple chevron shawl to practise increasing and decreasing in textured fabric. A basketweave cushion cover uses the same stitch construction but in a smaller, faster project. For a finer fabric with the same raised-square effect, try the pattern in DK weight on a 4mm hook.
